result:
The triangle-free setting rules out Solution 3 and Solution 2's bound is unsupported. For Solution 1 I rely on recall rather than a derivation, so my verdict on it is not certain.

**Solution 3.** Its extremal construction joins three classes cyclically, so any vertex from each class forms a triangle. The graph is therefore not triangle-free, and the construction does not show sharpness for this problem. The bound (n+5)/3 is also not a known result for the triangle-free case.

**Solution 2.** The balanced C₅ blow-up is triangle-free and has no rainbow C₄, but it only gives δᶜ = ⌊n/5⌋+1. That shows the threshold is at least about n/5, not that it equals (n+6)/5. The "upper bound" argument is a hand-wave with no proof, and the true threshold for large n is of order n/3, so (n+6)/5 is too small.

**Solution 1.** The order of magnitude (n+a)/3 is plausible. What I remember of the literature, in the work of Czygrinow, Molla, Nagle and Oursler and in related papers on rainbow C₄ in triangle-free edge-colored graphs, is the condition δᶜ(G) ≥ (n+2)/3, not (n+1)/3. I could not derive the constant independently, so this rests on memory and I am only moderately confident of it. On that basis, (n+1)/3 does not match the known sharp bound.

None of the three answers appears correct.

CHOICE: NONE
